questions.prompt: How does Swift's Automatic Reference Counting (ARC) manage class instance memory?

options.text: Compiler inserts retain/release reference-count operations deterministically at compile time, freeing instances when strong count hits 0

questions.prompt: When should you use `weak` vs `unowned` to break a retain cycle between class instances?

options.text: Use `weak` (Optional, auto-nil'd on dealloc) when the reference may become `nil` during its lifetime; use `unowned` only when guaranteed to never outlive the target

questions.prompt: Why do escaping closures often write `[weak self]` in their capture list?

options.text: To avoid a strong reference cycle if `self` owns the object/task holding the closure (and allow `self` to deallocate if no longer needed)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Swift `actor`s. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: External callers accessing an actor's mutable state or methods must `await` across the actor boundary
Actors allow synchronous external mutation of their `var` properties without `await`
Actors are reference types that protect their mutable state by serializing access (preventing data races)

questions.prompt: Match each Swift Concurrency primitive to its purpose.

columns.label: Runs a fixed number of child tasks concurrently in structured concurrency
Runs a dynamic number of child tasks concurrently and collects results
Isolates UI/main-thread state to the main serial executor

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `some Shape` (opaque type) and `any Shape` (existential type) in Swift 5.7+?

options.text: `some Shape` preserves a single concrete underlying type at compile time (static dispatch, supports `Self`/associated types); `any Shape` boxes heterogeneous types at runtime
`some Shape` allows mixing `Circle` and `Square` in one `[some Shape]` array

questions.prompt: What does the `Sendable` protocol signify in Swift Concurrency?

options.text: Values of the type can safely cross concurrency domains (actors/tasks) without data races

questions.prompt: What is actor reentrancy, and why does it matter after an `await` inside an `actor` method?

options.text: While an actor method is suspended at `await`, other callers can enter the actor and mutate state—so re-check assumptions after `await`!
Actors block the OS thread at `await`

questions.prompt: What does `Task.checkCancellation()` (or `Task.isCancelled`) do in structured concurrency?

options.text: Throws `CancellationError` if the current `Task` was cancelled, enabling cooperative early exit in long loops

questions.prompt: Why does `Task { ... }` inherit actor context whereas `Task.detached { ... }` does not?

options.text: `Task { ... }` inherits the enclosing actor (e.g., `@MainActor`) and priority; `Task.detached` starts with no actor isolation

questions.prompt: What is an `indirect enum` in Swift used for?

options.text: Recursive enums (like AST nodes or linked lists) where a case holds an instance of the enum itself via heap indirection

questions.prompt: What does `@propertyWrapper` allow in Swift?

options.text: Encapsulating reusable property storage/validation/observation logic (like `@Published`, `@AppStorage`, `@Clamped`) declaratively

questions.prompt: What is the Law of Exclusivity (memory exclusivity) enforced by Swift?

options.text: Two accesses to the same variable cannot overlap in time if at least one is a write (prevents aliasing bugs in `inout` and closures)

questions.prompt: Select all ways Swift avoids dynamic dispatch overhead in performance-critical code. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use `struct`s and `enum`s (value types have no subclass vtable dispatch)
Use generic `some Protocol` parameters instead of `any Protocol` existentials

questions.prompt: What does `ContiguousArray<T>` offer over `Array<T>` when bridging to Objective-C is not needed?

options.text: Guarantees contiguous native Swift buffer storage without Objective-C `NSArray` bridging checks on element access

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `withUnsafeContinuation` / `withCheckedContinuation`?

options.text: Bridging legacy callback/delegate APIs into Swift `async`/`await` (with `CheckedContinuation` trapping if resumed 0 or >1 times)

questions.prompt: What does `reserveCapacity(_:)` on `Array` or `Dictionary` optimize?

options.text: Pre-allocates buffer storage for a known element count, avoiding repeated geometric reallocations during `append`

questions.prompt: What does `nonisolated` on an `actor` method or computed property mean?

options.text: Opts that member out of actor isolation (safe when it only reads immutable `let` properties or `CustomStringConvertible` constants) so callers don't need `await`

questions.prompt: What does `MemoryLayout<T>.stride` represent vs `MemoryLayout<T>.size`?

options.text: `size` is the actual bytes of `T`; `stride` is `size` rounded up to `alignment` (distance between consecutive elements in an array)

questions.prompt: Match each Swift memory/pointer API to its safe usage rule.

columns.label: Borrows raw bytes only inside the closure scope (never escape the pointer)
Prevents ARC from deallocating a class instance early before a C/weak call finishes
Bridges callbacks to `async` while validating single-resume invariants

questions.prompt: What does `AsyncSequence` / `AsyncStream` model in Swift?

options.text: An asynchronous stream of values consumed sequentially with `for await item in stream`

questions.prompt: Why can `unowned` crash even if you think `self` outlives the closure?

options.text: If an async network/timer callback fires *after* the screen/object was dismissed and deallocated, dereferencing `unowned self` triggers a fatal trap

questions.prompt: What does `@unchecked Sendable` tell the Swift compiler?

options.text: Opts out of compiler `Sendable` verification—the author promises the type is thread-safe (e.g., via an internal lock/queue)

questions.prompt: What does `typed throws` (`func parse() throws(ParseError) -> AST` in Swift 6) add over untyped `throws`?

options.text: Encodes the exact error type in the function signature so callers catch `ParseError` exhaustively without `Any Error` casting

questions.prompt: Select all practices that prevent memory leaks and crashes in production Swift apps. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Store strong references from child objects back to parent controllers
Use `[weak self]` in long-lived or escaping async closures and delegate references (`weak var delegate`)
Avoid `!` force-unwraps and `try!` on external/network/user data
Use Instruments / Xcode Memory Graph Debugger or AddressSanitizer (`-sanitize=address`) to catch retain cycles and UAFs

questions.prompt: What happens if you block a Swift Concurrency cooperative thread pool thread with `Thread.sleep` or a synchronous semaphore `.wait()`?

options.text: It starves the limited cooperative thread pool and can deadlock if the awaited work needs a thread from the same pool

questions.prompt: What does `consuming` / `borrowing` parameter ownership modifiers (Swift 5.9+) allow?

options.text: Fine-grained control over ARC retain/release traffic and support for noncopyable types (`~Copyable`)

questions.prompt: What is a noncopyable struct (`struct FileHandle: ~Copyable`) useful for in Swift 5.9+?

options.text: Modeling unique ownership of OS resources (file descriptors, locks) where `deinit` runs deterministically and accidental copying is a compile error

questions.prompt: What does `os_signpost` / `OSSignposter` (Apple platforms) or `Logger` (`os.Logger`) provide over `print()`?

options.text: Structured, privacy-aware, low-overhead system logging and Instruments performance tracing

questions.prompt: What does `Mirror(reflecting: value)` do, and why should it be avoided in hot paths?

options.text: Performs runtime reflection over properties (useful for debugging/test assertions, but slow and allocation-heavy in hot loops)

questions.prompt: What do Swift Macros (`#Preview`, `@Observable`, `#expect`) introduced in Swift 5.9 do?

options.text: Transform parsed, type-checked Swift syntax trees at compile time in sandboxed compiler plugins

questions.prompt: What does `Array.withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer` allow without copying?

options.text: Direct contiguous pointer access to the array's backing storage for C FFI or SIMD loops within the closure

questions.prompt: Match each Swift concurrency hazard to its mitigation.

columns.label: Re-validate actor state invariants after resuming from `await`

questions.prompt: What does `Clock` / `ContinuousClock` / `SuspendingClock` (Swift 5.7+) improve for `Task.sleep` and timeouts?

options.text: Clean, testable time abstractions (`clock.sleep(for: .seconds(1))`) distinguishing monotonic uptime from wall-clock suspension

questions.prompt: Why should `NotificationCenter` observers or `Combine` `AnyCancellable`s be cleaned up or scoped to instance lifetime?

options.text: Forgotten block-based observers or retain-heavy sinks keep firing or leak memory after a view/service is dismissed

questions.prompt: What does `Swift Testing` (`@Test`, `#expect`, `#require`) improve over legacy `XCTest`?

options.text: Expressive `#expect(a == b)` failure diagnostics, parameterized `@Test(arguments:)`, and parallel execution by default

Expose all internal helper structs as `open`

questions.prompt: What does `Collection.firstIndex(where:)` return vs `Array[i]`?

options.text: `Index?` (`Optional<Index>`), which is `nil` if no element matches—avoiding out-of-bounds traps

questions.prompt: What is `@inlinable` in a Swift library module used for?

options.text: Exposes a small public function's body across module boundaries so callers can inline and specialize it

questions.prompt: What does `withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:)` do?

options.text: Runs an immediate `onCancel` hook when a `Task` is cancelled, ideal for aborting an underlying C/socket/URLSession operation

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to avoid accidental data races when migrating Swift 5 code to Swift 6 strict concurrency. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Make immutable data models `struct`s conforming to `Sendable`
Replace global `var` singletons with actor-isolated or `let` `Sendable` instances
Silence every warning with `nonisolated(unsafe)` without synchronization
Convert shared mutable classes to `actor`s or isolate UI classes to `@MainActor`

questions.prompt: Why is `precondition(index >= 0 && index < count)` better than returning a silent dummy value on internal API contract violations?

options.text: Failing fast on programmer-error invariants surfaces bugs immediately in testing rather than corrupting downstream state silently
